STL.Settings.LibraryPathHint: Where token art, frames, and the manifest live. The default is this module's persistent storage, which survives module updates. Changing this copies the library to the new location — one upload per file, so it can take a while for a large library.
STL.Settings.LibrarySourceHint: The file storage bucket the library folder belongs to. Leave as 'data' unless you are using S3 or a Forge asset library ('forgevtt').
STL.Settings.RingModeHint: How library art is turned into a token. Dynamic Ring lets Foundry draw its own ring around the artwork. Selected Frame composites the artwork onto a frame image ahead of time.
STL.Settings.FrameSrcHint: The frame image composited behind and around the artwork in Selected Token Frame mode. Ignored in Dynamic Token Ring mode.
STL.Settings.SubjectFitHint: How source artwork is framed before clipping. Art is clipped to a circle covering two thirds of the token, so fitting a tall full-body portrait whole lands that circle around the midriff. Fill from the top keeps the face.
STL.Settings.SubjectFitCoverTop: Fill, keep the top (best for full-body art)
STL.Settings.SubjectFitContain: Fit the whole image (art is already a square bust)
STL.Settings.MaskModeHint: How artwork is clipped before a ring or frame is applied. A square portrait dropped straight into a dynamic ring spills outside it, so clipping is on by default.
STL.Settings.RingMaskHint: Used when Subject Clipping is set to 'Custom mask image'. The artwork is kept wherever this image is opaque and erased where it is transparent, so a mask should be a solid shape on a transparent background. Tokenizer 2's masks under modules/tokenizer-2/img/masks/ work well.
STL.Settings.ThumbnailSizeHint: How large token images appear in the library browser. Larger sizes show fewer per row.
STL.Settings.RingScaleHint: How large the artwork sits inside the dynamic ring. Leave at 1 unless your art needs it: processing already clips the subject to the size Foundry's rings expect, so lowering this shrinks the art away from the ring rather than fitting it. Dynamic Token Ring mode only.
STL.Settings.RingColorHint: Hex colour for the dynamic ring, e.g. #c9a227. Leave blank to use the token's disposition colour.
STL.Settings.RingBackgroundHint: Hex colour for the dynamic ring's backdrop. Leave blank for the default.
STL.Settings.RingEffectsHint: Animated effect applied to the dynamic ring.
STL.Settings.ApplyPortrait: Use Portrait Art as Actor Avatar
STL.Settings.ApplyPortraitHint: When the art you apply has a portrait paired with it — the taller image it was cut from, sitting in the same folder — set that as the actor’s avatar. The token itself is unaffected. Images with no paired portrait leave the avatar alone either way.
STL.Settings.AutoApplyHint: When an actor has no saved library selection but its name matches a category, give new tokens a random image from that category. Only actors still using the default token artwork are touched.
STL.Settings.AutoApplyLinkedHint: Also auto-apply to linked actors (usually player characters). Off by default, since those normally have deliberately chosen artwork.
STL.Settings.ExportSizeHint: Pixel dimensions of composites produced in Selected Token Frame mode.
STL.Settings.ExportFormatHint: File format for composites. WebP is smaller; PNG is more widely compatible.
STL.Settings.DebugHint: Print verbose diagnostics to the browser console.
STL.Browser.Title: Token Library
STL.Browser.NoCategories: No categories yet. Add one, or drop art into the library's art folder.
STL.Browser.NoImages: No images match the current filter.
STL.Browser.NoFacets: This category has no traits to filter on yet.
STL.Browser.NoFacetsButUntagged: None of this category's images are tagged yet. Select some below and assign traits to make them filterable.
STL.Browser.SelectHint: Click a thumbnail to pin it; ctrl- or shift-click to select several for tagging.
STL.Browser.SeedDefaultsHint: Add the starter set of common D&D and Pathfinder NPC categories and traits. Existing entries are kept — this only fills in what is missing.
STL.Browser.ModeHint: Change this in the module settings
STL.Browser.NoFrameChosen: Selected Token Frame mode is active but no frame image is configured. Pick one in the module settings.
STL.Category.Title: Category & Traits
STL.Category.Label: Name
STL.Category.IdHint: Used as the folder name under art/. Leave blank to derive it from the name.
STL.Category.MatchNamesHint: Comma separated. An actor whose name contains any of these matches this category — so 'Bandit Captain' matches a 'bandit' entry.
STL.Category.CreatureTypesHint: Comma separated. Used only when no name matches.
STL.Category.FacetsHint: Traits are the filter dimensions shown in the browser. Races live here: add a 'race' trait and give it values. Traits are shared across every category.
STL.Category.DeleteMessage:
Remove {label} and its {count} image entries from the library?

The image files stay in your data folder — nothing is deleted from disk.
STL.Category.IdTaken: A category with the identifier "{id}" already exists. Edit that one instead, or choose another identifier.
STL.Import.Title: Add Images
STL.Import.NewValuesHint: These words appear in the filenames but are not known traits. Click one to add it as a trait value so it becomes filterable.
STL.Import.NeedCategory: Choose a category before adding images.
STL.Import.NoTokenizer: Tokenizer 2 is not available. Images will be added as-is; frame compositing is unavailable.
STL.Remove.Title: Remove from Library
STL.Remove.RestoreHint: Bring back every image previously removed from this category.
STL.Tag.Hint: Tick every value that applies — traits you don't touch are left alone.
STL.Tag.WillWrite: This trait will be written to the selected images.
STL.Tag.SkippedReadOnly: Skipped {count} art-pack image(s) — art packs are read-only.
STL.Tag.NothingChosen: Click a trait value first — nothing has been changed.
STL.Tag.NoFacets: No traits are defined yet. Add one to start tagging.
STL.Tag.NoValues: No values yet — add some in the category editor.

Resume it now?

STL.Traits.Title: Traits
STL.Traits.Hint: Traits are shared by every category. The number beside a value is how many images carry it — a value on nothing is safe to remove, a value on hundreds is not.
STL.Traits.NoValues: No values yet — add some below.
STL.Traits.NewValuePlaceholder: New value, or several separated by commas
STL.Traits.IdFixed: A trait’s id is fixed once created, because images are tagged against it.
STL.Traits.UsedHint: Images carrying any value of this trait
STL.Traits.RemoveTraitMessage:
Remove {label}?

{count} image(s) carry a value of it. The images keep their tags, but the trait stops appearing as a filter until it is defined again.
STL.Traits.RemoveValueMessage:
Remove {value}?

{count} image(s) carry it. They keep the tag, but it stops being offered as a filter.
STL.Traits.DuplicateId: Two traits share the id "{id}". Ids must be unique.
